chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Aban, from Fazl Abu al-Abbas, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is the man more deserving of his child, or the woman?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but the man. So if the woman says to her husband who divorced her,
I will breastfeed my son for a wage similar to what you would find [paid] to the one who would breastfeed him,' then she is more deserving of it.
ai.seo_question: Who has custody of the child after divorce in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential hierarchy of child custody, establishing the father as the default guardian while recognizing the mother's superior claim if she provides comparable breastfeeding services. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the mother's physical nurturing role as a decisive factor in custody disputes, balancing paternal authority with maternal care. The exception underscores the practical consideration of the child's welfare, a principle deeply rooted in Islamic family law.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Aban, from Fazl Abu Al Abbas who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is the man more deserving with his son or the woman?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but the man. So if the woman says to her husband who had divorced her,
‘I will breast-feed my son with similar to what you would find the one who would breast-feed him, so she would be more rightful with it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-ffassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Aban from Fadl abu al-‘Abbas who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if a man has more right for the custody of a child or woman. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, the man has more right.
If a divorced woman asks for breastfeeding her child for the same price as others,
then she has more right for breastfeeding.’”
